producer_report.summary: The drain now asks a new default-no-op hook, Steps::commit_records(job), right after Steps::land answers Landed. It runs inside Drain::land, while the job still holds the head of the landing queue (the LandingSlot is held until attempts end, and await_head lets only the head reach Drain::land). So with several jobs in flight, records commits follow landing order, each after its own landing and before the next. A job that did not land never reaches the hook. A failing hook is noted in Report::notes and printed, and the landing still counts. With the default hook, a bound of 1, or plain drain, behaviour is unchanged. The real steps keep the default. go still commits a job's records at close, so moving that commit into the queue is later work. The CHANGELOG, the design note and the doc comments all say this. I added a records_order test module to tests/drain.rs. Its stub commits real priority records through the real Committer, and the tests drive drain_concurrent. They cover: three jobs in flight landing and recording in the order c, a, b; append-only with a rejected fourth job; a refused commit not undoing the landing; the bound-1 sequence through drain_concurrent and drain; and a default-hook stub at bound 2. They print the sequences for three jobs. The changes are in drain.rs, the tests, CHANGELOG.md and docs/design/async-drain.md. Nothing was removed from existing files.

open_issues: The real steps keep the default no-op hook. go still commits a job's closing files and its Score and Outcome records at close (crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs, land_or_block), before the job joins the landing queue. Moving that commit into the queue slot changes the run path and is outside this job's files. The CHANGELOG, design note and doc comments say so. Do you want it as a follow-up?

Design section 8 also says failed or closed jobs commit through the queue. Acceptance criterion 2 says no record for a job that did not land, so I followed the criterion. Failed-job routing is left to a later job.
The month-shard append-only conflict reading is not confirmed; per-job record files are new paths. The design note says so.

The hook test proves the order and that the call is made while the job holds the head slot. It does not prove the call sits inside the landing mutex, because a call moved to just after Drain::land returns would also keep the order; the test names and design note do not claim more.

No max_in_flight parameter exists on drain_concurrent (that is build job 10), so the max_in_flight 1 pins use bounds 1 and 2 of [parallel] max_concurrency. The default-hook test at bound 2 uses a stub with no repository, so 'no commit made' is shown by the log and notes, not by a repository check.
I did not run the full workspace cargo test (about 10 minutes); Athena's own run covers it.
mistakes: I read a very large span of tests/drain.rs to find the file end, which cost budget; a Grep count for the line total would have been enough.
learnings: A lone priority record (athena.priority/1) commits through Committer::commit_records and the gate with no extra records, and Records::load reads a job with only a priority record.
Git, StateDir and Committer are Sync enough to live inside a Steps + Sync stub, so the stub can make real gated commits from the drain's worker threads.
drain_concurrent's fourth argument is [parallel] max_concurrency, not max_in_flight, which only the disk guard in go reads.
A rejected job is retried once, so a stub that lists a job as failing sees a '<job>-retry' run, and the drain ends RepeatedFailure after the in-flight jobs finish.
desires: A way to run a single targeted test without the 126 s full drain test binary would have helped; the targeted filter worked fine.
